framework.primary: Python + NumPy/SciPy (scipy.linalg.solve_banded / scipy.sparse for the banded M-matrix and generalized-Jacobian solves)
framework.reasoning: This is a numerical PDE / finite-difference scheme paper, not a neural-network paper. All linear algebra is 1D banded (tridiagonal/pentadiagonal) systems solved exactly at O(n) cost -- scipy.linalg.solve_banded is the direct match for the paper's repeated claim of 'one banded M-matrix solve at O(n) cost'. No GPU, no autograd, no dataset loader are needed. matplotlib is used for the two paper figures (coverage thresholds, limiter localization).

module_hierarchy.description: Active-set semismooth-Newton solver (Eqs. 24-26, Proposition 5, Lemma 2). Warm-starts from the unlimited solve; if not nonnegative, iterates clamp-pattern updates, each one banded solve. Includes an explicit runtime nonsingularity/iteration-cap safeguard because Proposition 5's general mixed-pattern nonsingularity above gamma_pic is an OPEN question in the paper (SIR implementation_assumption #4) -- NOT a proved guarantee, so the solver must not assume unconditional convergence.

tensor_flows.name: FCDF-B single implicit step (Proposition 1)
steps: p = b.copy()  # p^[0] = b, Eq. 14
for sweep in range(max_sweeps):
d = op.unlimited_flux(p)                      # Eq. 9
Lambda = limiter.clamp(d, b, gamma)            # Eq. 15 / clamp form Eq. A.2
rhs = b + gamma * divergence(Lambda)           # Eq. 13-14 assembled RHS
p_new = op.core_solve(rhs, gamma)              # (I-gamma*A1)^-1 rhs, banded solve
if ||p_new - p||_1 < tol: p = p_new; break
p = p_new
return p  # nonnegative, mass-conservative by Proposition 1(i)-(ii)

tensor_flows.name: FCDF-DC one full time step (Proposition 3)
steps: Y0 = FCDF_B_step_with_offset(op, limiter, base=p_n, offset=0, gamma=dt)   # Eq. 17, predictor
w = op.apply_A2(Y0)
G = (dt**2/2) * flux_of(op.apply_A2(w))    # defect flux, Section 4.2
p_next = FCDF_B_step_with_offset(op, limiter, base=p_n, offset=G, gamma=dt)  # Eq. 18, corrector
return p_next  # 2nd-order in time where caps are slack, Proposition 3(iv)

tensor_flows.name: Active-set solve (Proposition 5)
steps: p_unlimited = solve_banded(I - gamma*A2, b)   # try the unlimited system first
if p_unlimited >= 0 (elementwise, tolerance): return p_unlimited, pattern_updates=0
else: label each interface's clamp pattern from p_unlimited
for update in range(max_pattern_updates):
V_S = I - gamma*(A1 + C_restricted_to_free_interfaces(pattern))   # Eq. 25-26
p = solve_banded(V_S, adjusted_rhs(pattern, b))
new_pattern = relabel(p)
if new_pattern == pattern: break   # F is piecewise-linear -> terminates on pattern match
pattern = new_pattern
return p  # nonnegative by construction since any zero of F is a Prop.1(i) fixed point

risk_assessment.risk: gamma_0 / gamma_r linear-window thresholds cannot be cross-checked against the (unavailable) companion paper's closed form.
risk_assessment.description: SIR ambiguity #1 / implementation_assumption #1: only the bisection-on-resolvent-sign procedure is specified in this paper. If the bisection search bracket or tolerance differs from the authors', the exact threshold values in Table 2 may not reproduce to full precision, though the qualitative coverage conclusion (condition (a) holds from n=101, condition (b) never holds) should still reproduce.
risk_assessment.mitigation: Implement bisection with a wide default bracket (1e-8, 1e6) and report both the threshold and a coverage-condition boolean; treat exact threshold digits as approximate, not exact, in any comparison report.

risk_assessment.risk: Active-set solver's mixed-pattern nonsingularity is an open question above gamma_pic (Proposition 5).
risk_assessment.description: A pathological pattern could in principle produce a singular or ill-conditioned V_S for gamma>gamma_pic; the paper only reports empirical non-failure.
risk_assessment.mitigation: Wrap each banded solve in a condition-number / LinAlgError guard; if a solve fails, fall back to halving the pattern-update step or reporting non-convergence rather than crashing or silently returning garbage.

risk_assessment.risk: Sign-changing drift (OU benchmark) stencil at/near the sign-change node is not spelled out explicitly.
risk_assessment.description: SIR ambiguity #4: the paper states mu>0 stencils and says mu<0 is 'fully symmetric' and sign-changing drift is handled 'directionally at each node' without giving the exact per-node rule.
risk_assessment.mitigation: Implement per-node upwind selection based on the sign of mu at each node (or interface-averaged mu), matching the donor-node convention already given for the Zalesak rule (j=i for d>0, j=i+1 for d<0); unit-test mass conservation (1^T A2 = 0) and unconditional-positivity-of-core (A1 remains an M-matrix) hold under this convention before trusting downstream results.

risk_assessment.risk: No numeric Picard/Newton convergence tolerance is stated in the paper.
risk_assessment.description: SIR implementation_assumption #6: achieved residuals of ~1e-13 to 1e-15 are reported but not a target tolerance.
risk_assessment.mitigation: Default tol=1e-12 on the l1 sweep-increment norm; expose as a config value; confirm reproduced residuals land in the same 1e-13 to 1e-15 ballpark as Tables 8-9 before trusting exact match.

risk_assessment.risk: Sub-cell boundary-mass-accumulation regime (Proposition 2 caveat) is outside nodal L1 assessment.
risk_assessment.description: If a benchmark configuration drives the boundary-layer width below h, nodal L1 comparisons saturate at O(1) regardless of scheme correctness -- not a bug.
risk_assessment.mitigation: None of the reproduced benchmarks (OU, smooth advection, front) enter this regime at the tested D values, so this is documented as a known limitation in the README rather than specially handled in code.
